title: 영어브리핑_2026-10-27
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: Asanka 11/15 출발 기준 입사일·봉제실장 공백(10/31~) 대책 법인장 보고, Aritzia 실(COATS) 세관 미신고 건 Trinh Do 사실 확인 후 법인장·박부장 보고, 11월 기계임대 리스트 김홍기 사원 송부(10/27 기한). 지난주 시험 8/16점(정답률 50%, 10/24 채점분 정식 반영). 10/26(월) 07:20 작성이라 월요일 업무는 미반영(10/24 토 이후 메일 없음, 아침점검 10/24 기준).
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Tuesday, October twenty-seventh. Yesterday was Monday, and this week has a heavy Friday and Saturday ahead.

This briefing has eight parts. Part one is the opening, which you are hearing now. Part two is the top three for today. Part three is reports to collect. Part four is replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines. Part six is an English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.

One note before we start. The mail record I could read ends on Saturday afternoon. No new mail from Monday was visible to me. So some items below may already be done. If so, just skip them and move on.
Please listen slowly. When you hear a pause, say the sentence out loud. Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The sewing manager gap, and Asanka's start date.

What is happening? Chamin, the current sewing manager, leaves this Saturday, October thirty-first. Asanka, the new sewing manager, replied on Saturday. He sent his photo for the e-visa. He said he will be ready to depart on November fifteenth. Channa, the factory manager, had asked for an early November start. That is no longer possible.

Why does it matter? The sewing floor will have no manager for about two weeks. Channa is not in Da Nang either. And on Friday, Kasun from Aritzia visits the factory to check quality. This is the biggest risk this week.

Your first action today. Report to Mr Moon. Tell him the realistic start date is mid-November, after the visa and flight are fixed. Propose who covers the sewing floor during the gap. Ms Lai, the sewing manager under Chamin, is the natural choice for the lines. Sateesh covers quality for the Kasun visit. Then share the same message with Channa and with Harry Heo at head office. After that, reply to Asanka. Confirm that his arrival airport is Da Nang, and ask him to send his flight details as soon as he books.
Number two. Aritzia thread imported without a customs declaration.

What is happening? On Saturday, Trinh Do from the export-import team reported a problem. A few shipments of Aritzia thread from Coats Phong Phu arrived at our warehouse. But the invoices were issued to Poongin Trading, not to PI Vina Danang. So these shipments were never declared to customs on our side.

Why does it matter? Our customs ledger must match what is in the warehouse. This Saturday we do the physical count of fabric and thread. Mr Moon also just sent head office the notice about the new customs ledger control. Any thread in the warehouse with no declaration will show up as a discrepancy. Customs can treat this as non-compliance.

Your first action today. Do not decide alone, and do not guess the rule. First, get the facts from Trinh Do. How many shipments, how many cones or kilograms, which dates, and whether the thread is already used in production. Then report to Mr Moon and Mr Park with the facts and two or three options. Only after that, decide on the next step with customs.
Number three. The November machine rental list for head office.

What is happening? Ian Kim at head office needs the November rental list by today, Tuesday. On Saturday you tidied the list yourself and sent it to Mr Moon for approval. You also asked Hao from the maintenance team two questions by Monday morning. Why do we need three computer sewing machines, and what is the purchase price per unit.
Why does it matter? This is a head office deadline. If it is late, the rental for November may not be arranged in time.

Your first action today. Check two things in your inbox. Did Hao answer the two questions, and did Mr Moon approve. If both are done, send the list to Ian Kim before lunch. If Hao has not answered, call Mr Mai, the maintenance manager, and get the answer by phone.
Part three. Reports to collect.
Here are the reports you should chase today. For each one, I will give you one English sentence you can use.

First, Hao, maintenance statistics. The two points about the computer sewing machines. The deadline was Monday morning. Say: "Ms Hao, I still need the reason for three units and the price per unit. Please reply by ten o'clock."

Second, Mai from purchasing. Three items are open with her. One, the sewing building electricity invoice for the second period of October. It should be in the shared folder. Two, the two roof points you asked about on Saturday. The torn roof above the fabric spreading machine, and the leak in the boiler roof, with photos. Three, the relaxing shelves. She counted the thirty-nine shelves with the warehouse team. Now she needs to get quotations for the covers, the torn vinyl, and the repainting. Say: "Mai, thank you for the shelf count. Please get two quotations based on these quantities by Thursday."

Third, Mr Mai, the maintenance manager. There is no rain in the forecast this week. You asked him to repair the four leaking points, two gutters, the material warehouse roof, and the boiler roof, during this dry week. Say: "Mr Mai, which of the four leaking points are finished? Please send photos of each one."

Fourth, Linh and Mint. The broken pallets. You asked them to find only the badly broken pallets, not to check every pallet. Mr Moon wants the usable ones kept. The result is due by Saturday. Say: "Ms Linh, how many badly broken pallets have you found so far? Please send the photos by area."

Fifth, Mr Tam, the CAD room leader. Tuesday is one of your two check days for the CAD daily report. On Saturday you sent him a strong reminder with Mr Park and Channa in copy, and you met him with Yumi as interpreter. Today, open the file yourself. Check the Leader Summary line and the pattern loan log. Say: "Mr Tam, I checked the file this morning. The leader summary for yesterday is still missing. Please fill it in by five thirty today."

Sixth, Trinh Tran, the chief accountant. Two items are due today. The accounting team R and R update, and the first November CM application. Also, several purchase requests have been waiting in the approval box for a long time. Say: "Ms Trinh, could you confirm whether the R and R file will be ready today?"

Seventh, Hoang from HR. Today is the payment day for short-term contract salaries for October. You decided not to wait for a reply, but check that the payment file is final. Say: "Ms Hoang, is the short-term payroll final and ready for payment today?"

Eighth, Quan from IT. He finished the monitor list in the IT asset register, with labels on all monitors. Dieu's email account is still not created. He contacted Jun Kim at head office again. Say: "Mr Quan, thank you for the monitors. Please let me know when Dieu's account is ready."
Part four. Replies you owe.

First, Trinh Do, about the thread without customs declaration. She asked you to check and advise the next steps. Do not advise yet. Ask for facts. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for reporting this early. Before we decide, I'd like to understand the full picture." Then list your questions, number of shipments, quantities, dates, and current use.

Second, Asanka. He sent his photo and said November fifteenth. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for the photo. We will proceed with the e-visa now." Then ask him to confirm Da Nang as the arrival airport, and to send the ticket as soon as he books it.

Third, Ms Tho from HR, about the GOH box loading supplier. GOH means garments on hanger. The supplier quoted a much higher price per box. Ms Tho did not agree, and the supplier will send a revised quotation after the next GOH loading in mid-November. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you, Ms Tho. I agree with your decision." Then say we will compare the revised quotation with our current cost per box after the November loading.

Fourth, Mai, about the shelf quantities. She answered on Saturday morning. Your reply gives the next step, two quotations with the same scope, by Thursday. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for checking the thirty-nine shelves with the warehouse team."
Fifth, Quan, about the IT asset register. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for completing the monitor list." Then ask what items remain in the register, and when he can finish them.

Sixth, Ian Kim at head office. Once Mr Moon approves, send the rental list with a short note in Korean. Mention the change from October, fewer rental units, and the separate purchase request for machines.
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Tuesday, October twenty-seventh. Three deadlines. The November machine rental list to Ian Kim. The short-term contract salary payment. And the accounting R and R update with the first November CM application. Tuesday is also your needle order day. Prepare the Groz-Beckert order file for Chloe Kim, so the CEO can approve it on Wednesday. And one check from yesterday. The weekly firewood report to Chloe Kim was due Monday. Please confirm it went out, including the thirty percent of wood that was returned because the pieces were too thin.
Wednesday, October twenty-eighth. Your calendar has the monthly stock status update for the planning team.
Thursday, October twenty-ninth. Your calendar has the next-week overtime report. Also, do the pre-check with the export-import team and the warehouse for Saturday's count.

Friday, October thirtieth. Kasun from Aritzia visits for a quality check. Thao from the MR team also planned a J.Crew pre-production meeting that day. Two more deadlines. The completion report for the information security pledge from local staff, and the third quarter corporate income tax prepayment.
Saturday, October thirty-first. The physical count of fabric and thread. And it is Chamin's last working day. On Friday afternoon, make sure the handover notes and his company items are collected.
Part six. English review.
Today we review twelve expressions. The first four are the ones you missed on Saturday's test. Then expressions from yesterday's card. Say each one with me.

The expression is "log". It means to record a result or a number, usually in a file or a sheet. For example, "Please log the roller temperature during the test." Now say it with me. Please log the roller temperature during the test. ... ... ... One more time. Please log the roller temperature during the test. ... ... ...

The expression is "comply with". It means to follow a rule or a standard. For example, "The new chemical complies with the buyer's restricted substances list." Now say it with me. The new chemical complies with the buyer's list. ... ... ... One more time. The new chemical complies with the buyer's list. ... ... ...

The expression is "feasible". It means possible to do in real conditions. For example, "Please let me know if this sheet is feasible on the floor." Now say it with me. Please let me know if this sheet is feasible on the floor. ... ... ... One more time. Please let me know if this sheet is feasible on the floor. ... ... ...

The expression is "outstanding". Here it means not yet done, not yet submitted. For example, "The photos and the quotation are still outstanding." Now say it with me. The photos and the quotation are still outstanding. ... ... ... One more time. The photos and the quotation are still outstanding. ... ... ...

The expression is "discrepancy". It means a difference between two records that should match. For example, "There is a discrepancy between the customs ledger and the warehouse count." Now say it with me. There is a discrepancy between the customs ledger and the warehouse count. ... ... ... One more time. There is a discrepancy between the customs ledger and the warehouse count. ... ... ...

The expression is "proceed with". It means to go ahead with a plan or a step. For example, "We will proceed with the e-visa now." Now say it with me. We will proceed with the e-visa now. ... ... ... One more time. We will proceed with the e-visa now. ... ... ...

The expression is "prevent". It means to stop a problem before it happens. For example, "A fixed team will prevent size mistakes during loading." Now say it with me. A fixed team will prevent size mistakes during loading. ... ... ... One more time. A fixed team will prevent size mistakes during loading. ... ... ...

The expression is "address", as a verb. It means to deal with a question or a problem. For example, "Only question number one has been addressed so far." Now say it with me. Only question number one has been addressed so far. ... ... ... One more time. Only question number one has been addressed so far. ... ... ...

The expression is "revised". It means changed and updated. For example, "The supplier will send a revised quotation after the next loading." Now say it with me. The supplier will send a revised quotation after the next loading. ... ... ... One more time. The supplier will send a revised quotation after the next loading. ... ... ...

The pattern is "Going forward, please ...". It means from now on, please do it this way. For example, "Going forward, please write the PO numbers in every cost PR." Now say it with me. Going forward, please write the PO numbers in every cost PR. ... ... ... One more time. Going forward, please write the PO numbers in every cost PR. ... ... ...

The pattern is "I understand your concern about ..., but ...". It means I hear your worry, and here is my point. For example, "I understand your concern about the workload, but the EXIM team will handle this." Now say it with me. I understand your concern about the workload, but the EXIM team will handle this. ... ... ... One more time. I understand your concern about the workload, but the EXIM team will handle this. ... ... ...

The pattern is "I'd like to understand why ... before ...". It means I want the reason first, then I will decide. For example, "I'd like to understand why the invoices went to head office before we contact customs." Now say it with me. I'd like to understand why the invoices went to head office before we contact customs. ... ... ... One more time. I'd like to understand why the invoices went to head office before we contact customs. ... ... ...
Remember the coach's advice from Saturday. After "whether", "once", and "until", put a subject and a verb right away. Who does it, and what do they do.
Part seven. Role-play.
Today's situation. It is Tuesday morning. You go to the export-import office to talk with Trinh Do about the Aritzia thread. Listen first. Then we repeat two key sentences.
Anthony: Ms Trinh, thank you for your report on Saturday about the Aritzia thread. Before we decide anything, I'd like to understand the full picture.
Trinh Do: Of course, Mr Lee. We found three invoices. All of them were issued to Poongin Trading, not to our company.
Anthony: Could you confirm whether the thread actually arrived in our warehouse?
Trinh Do: Yes. The warehouse received all of it. Some of it is already on the sewing lines.
Anthony: I see. So we have a discrepancy. The customs ledger shows nothing, but the warehouse has the thread. How many cones in total, and on which dates?
Trinh Do: I will prepare a list with the dates, the quantities, and the current stock. I can send it by eleven.
Anthony: Good. Please include which styles used the thread. I'd like to understand why the invoices went to head office before we contact customs.
Trinh Do: I think the buyer's nominated supplier used the old billing address. I will ask the MR team to check with Coats.
Anthony: Please do. One more thing. Going forward, please check the invoice name on every nominated material before it enters the warehouse.
Trinh Do: Understood, Mr Lee. I will also brief Thu Hien, since she handles the import report.
Anthony: Thank you. I will report to Mr Moon and Mr Park this afternoon with your list. We will decide the next step together.
Now, two key sentences. Say them with me.
First. Could you confirm whether the thread actually arrived in our warehouse? ... ... ... One more time. Could you confirm whether the thread actually arrived in our warehouse? ... ... ...

Second. I'd like to understand why the invoices went to head office before we contact customs. ... ... ... One more time. I'd like to understand why the invoices went to head office before we contact customs. ... ... ...
Part eight. Closing.

Here is today in one sentence. Report the Asanka start date and the sewing floor cover plan to Mr Moon, get the facts on the undeclared thread from Trinh Do, and send the November rental list to Ian Kim before lunch.
Have a good Tuesday, Anthony. See you on Wednesday.
